definitions.explanation: Small, soft green plants that grow in dense mats on rocks, trees, and damp ground.

examples.english: Moss is growing on the stone.

examples.japanese: {苔|こけ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}えた→生える：02392_haeru⟧⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧。
examples.english: A garden covered with moss is beautiful.

examples.japanese: ⟦{転|ころ}がる→転がる：02571_korogaru⟧⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{苔|こけ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}えない→生える：02392_haeru⟧。
examples.english: A rolling stone gathers no moss. (Proverb)
examples.notes: Japanese version of the English proverb

examples.japanese: ⟦{雨上|あめあ}がり→雨上がり：14586_ameagari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{森|もり}→森：02260_mori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{苔|こけ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美|うつく}しい→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧⟦{緑色|みどりいろ}→緑色：24190_midoriiro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{輝|かがや}いている→輝く：02032_kagayaku⟧。
examples.english: In the forest after rain, the moss shines in a beautiful green.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{西芳寺|さいほうじ}→西芳寺：noentry⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{苔寺|こけでら}→苔寺：noentry⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧、⟦{境内|けいだい}→境内：12095_keidai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覆|おお}う→覆う：02020_oou⟧{苔|こけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{美|うつく}しさ→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られています→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Saihoji Temple in Kyoto is also called the Moss Temple and is known for the beauty of moss covering its grounds.

notes:
Moss carries strong aesthetic associations in Japan — age, stillness, and the beauty of things that take time (⟦{侘|わ}び{寂|さ}び→侘び寂び：11691_wabisabi⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苔|こけ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}える→生える：02392_haeru⟧ - moss grows (on something)
- {苔|こけ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{覆|おお}われる→覆う：02020_oou⟧ - to be covered in moss
- {苔|こけ}⟦むす→生す：noentry⟧ - to become mossy with age (literary; the phrase in the national anthem, 「{苔|こけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧むす⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧」, means 'until the stones grow moss')

TYPES:
- ⟦{蘚類|せんるい}→蘚類：noentry⟧ (true mosses)
- ⟦{苔類|たいるい}→苔類：noentry⟧ (liverworts)
- ⟦{地衣類|ちいるい}→地衣類：27746_chiirui⟧ (lichens - often lumped in colloquially)

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{苔玉|こけだま}→苔玉：noentry⟧ (moss ball, a decorative planting)
- ⟦{苔寺|こけでら}→苔寺：noentry⟧ (moss temple, the nickname of ⟦{西芳寺|さいほうじ}→西芳寺：noentry⟧ in Kyoto)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Moss is cultivated rather than removed in a ⟦{日本庭園|にほんていえん}→日本庭園：19199_nihonteien⟧, where a {苔|こけ}-covered ⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧ or ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧ signals a garden that has been tended for generations. Note that the English proverb 'a rolling stone gathers no moss' is used in Japanese with the same wording but often the opposite reading: for many speakers it praises the moss, not the motion.
